title: The cost of the road not taken

blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Define opportunity cost precisely, and separate it from the money cost of a choice and from the list of everything given up.

blocks.heading: What opportunity cost means
blocks.text: Every choice closes a door. When a farmer in the Otavi area plants one field with maize, the same field cannot carry the sunflower crop it might have carried instead. Opportunity cost is the benefit lost from the next best alternative that is given up when a choice is made: the maize is chosen, and the harvest the sunflowers would have yielded is the cost. Two rules make the definition precise. First, the cost is the next best alternative, not all the alternatives forgone stacked together - the farmer considered sunflowers and Lucerne hay, but once sunflowers ranked second, hay drops out of the reckoning. Second, the opportunity cost is not the money spent. If the maize seed cost N$2 000, that is the money cost; the opportunity cost is the sunflower harvest forgone, which money may not measure at all.

blocks.heading: Why the cost exists at all
blocks.text: Opportunity cost exists because resources are scarce. A field, a worker's morning, a government's budget rand: each can serve one use at a time, so using it one way means not using it another. If resources were abundant enough for every purpose, choosing would sacrifice nothing and opportunity cost would vanish. This is why the idea sits at the centre of the subject: it is the economic problem of topic 1.1 translated into a number - the measured benefit of what the choice gave up. A student in Japan choosing between two hours of extra mathematics and two hours at a part-time job that pays 2 400 yen faces the same structure: the time is scarce, and the pay forgone is the cost of the study.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: Opportunity cost is the working form of the economic problem from topic 1.1, and topic 1.4 draws it as the production possibility curve, where moving along the boundary shows the output of one good given up for another.
